# UGR test fixtures

Test data for the UGR (Unified Glare Rating) tabular method from
CIE 117:1995 and CIE 190:2010.

## Source and license

The sample luminaires and the Relux, DIALux and CIE 190 reference tables come
from [eulumdat-ugr](https://github.com/123VincentB/eulumdat-ugr) (commit
`9f60147`), files `data/input/sample_01..11.ldt` and
`data/reference/ugr_table_*.csv`. eulumdat-ugr is released under the MIT
license, Copyright (c) 2026 123VincentB. The copyright notice and the license
text are in [LICENSE](../../../LICENSE).

eulumdat-ugr does not say where the data originally came from. What the files
show:

- `sample_01` to `sample_10` are anonymized measurement files. The company is
  `company`, names and file names are replaced with `sample_NN`, but report
  numbers, dates and initials remain. The original manufacturers are not named.
- `sample_11` is dated `10.03.2010/CIE` and is the example luminaire of
  CIE 190:2010. `ugr_table_11_cie190.csv` holds that publication's UGR table.
- `ugr_table_NN_Relux.csv` and `ugr_table_NN_Dialux.csv` are values computed by
  the Relux and DIALux lighting software.

The `*_python.csv` files were generated by `reference/generate_python.py` with
eulumdat-ugr 1.0.2, eulumdat-luminance 1.3.1 and eulumdat-py 1.0.0 (all MIT,
123VincentB). That script shows how to regenerate them.

## Files

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `sample_NN.ldt` | Sample luminaires 01 to 11. `sample_11.ldt` is the CIE 190:2010 example luminaire. |
| `reference/ugr_table_NN_Relux.csv` | UGR table exported from Relux, 1 decimal. |
| `reference/ugr_table_NN_Dialux.csv` | UGR table exported from DIALux, 1 decimal. |
| `reference/ugr_table_11_cie190.csv` | UGR table published in CIE 190:2010, 1 decimal. |
| `reference/ugr_table_NN_python.csv` | Unrounded `UgrResult.values` from eulumdat-ugr, 4 decimals. |
| `reference/luminance_NN_python.csv` | `LuminanceResult.at()` and `projected_area()` samples from eulumdat-luminance. |

## UGR table format

`ugr_table_*.csv` files have no header and hold 19 rows × 10 columns of
comma-separated values. The Relux and DIALux exports may omit the final
newline, and Relux writes `<10.0` for values below 10.

Rows are the standard CIE 190 rooms, given as X × Y in multiples of the
mounting height H (X across the line of sight, Y along it):

| Row | X | Y | Row | X | Y | Row | X | Y |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 2H | 2H | 7 | 4H | 3H | 14 | 8H | 8H |
| 1 | 2H | 3H | 8 | 4H | 4H | 15 | 8H | 12H |
| 2 | 2H | 4H | 9 | 4H | 6H | 16 | 12H | 4H |
| 3 | 2H | 6H | 10 | 4H | 8H | 17 | 12H | 6H |
| 4 | 2H | 8H | 11 | 4H | 12H | 18 | 12H | 8H |
| 5 | 2H | 12H | 12 | 8H | 4H | | | |
| 6 | 4H | 2H | 13 | 8H | 6H | | | |

Columns 0–4 are crosswise (luminaire axis across the line of sight) and
columns 5–9 are endwise (luminaire axis along the line of sight). Within each
orientation the reflectance order (ceiling/walls/working plane, in %) is:

| Column | Reflectances |
| --- | --- |
| 0, 5 | 70/50/20 |
| 1, 6 | 70/30/20 |
| 2, 7 | 50/50/20 |
| 3, 8 | 50/30/20 |
| 4, 9 | 30/30/20 |

## Luminance sample format

`luminance_NN_python.csv` has the header
`c_deg,gamma_deg,luminance_cd_m2,projected_area_m2`. Each row samples one
(C, γ) direction from `LuminanceCalculator.compute(ldt, full=True)`:

- `luminance_cd_m2`: `LuminanceResult.at(c_deg, gamma_deg)`, in cd/m²
- `projected_area_m2`: `LuminanceResult.projected_area(c_deg, gamma_deg)`, in m²

The sampled angles are C ∈ {0, 12, 30, 90, 200, 352.5} and
γ ∈ {0, 45, 65, 67, 85}. Some of these lie between the file's grid angles, so
the samples also cover bilinear interpolation and the C wrap-around past 345°.
